inlines.v: RAMP, verb intransitive [See Ramble and Romance.] 1. To climb, as a plant; to creep up. Plants furnished with tendrils catch hold, and so ramping on trees, they mount to a great height. 2. To spring; to leap; to bound; to prance; to frolic. Their bridles they would champ - and trampling the fine element, would fiercely ramp Sporting the lion ramp'd. [In the latter sense, the word is usually written and pronounced romp; the word being originally pronounced with a broad.] RAMP, noun A leap; a spring; a bound.
